title: T1490: Inhibit System Recovery
summary: Adversaries delete or disable recovery features so that encrypted or corrupted systems cannot be restored, converting a recoverable incident into an extended clinical outage.
content:
## T1490 - Inhibit System Recovery

The technique described here is documented across intrusions affecting the health sector. Adversaries delete or disable recovery features so that encrypted or corrupted systems cannot be restored, converting a recoverable incident into an extended clinical outage.

**Tactic:** Impact

**Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS, Network Devices

## Healthcare context

Where recovery is inhibited, restoration timelines extend from hours to weeks, which is the difference between a managed downtime procedure and diversion of emergency services.

## Detection

Shadow copy deletion commands; modification or deletion of backup catalogues; disabling of recovery boot options; backup repository authentication from an unexpected account.

## Mitigations

- Hold at least one backup copy offline or immutable, beyond the reach of a domain-privileged account.
- Alert on shadow copy deletion as a high-priority event.
- Separate backup infrastructure credentials from the production identity domain.

## Observations

- Backups reachable with domain credentials are within the blast radius of the intrusion and cannot be counted as recovery capability.
- This technique is what converts an incident into a crisis, and it is usually executed in the final minutes.
- Immutability at the storage layer is more reliable than access control at the application layer.
